segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: We make known to you, brothers and sisters, the grace of God that has been given in the assemblies of Macedonia:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: amid a severe test of affliction, their overflowing joy and their deep poverty overflowed into the wealth of their generosity.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For according to their means, I testify, and beyond their means, they gave of their own accord,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: begging us with much urging for the favor of sharing in the service to the holy ones—

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and not just as we had hoped, but they gave themselves first to the Lord and to us, through the will of God,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: so that we urged Titus that, just as he had already made a beginning, so he should also complete this act of grace among you.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But just as you overflow in everything—in faith and speech and knowledge and all earnestness and the love from us that is in you—see that you overflow in this act of grace too.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I am not saying this as a command; rather, through the earnestness of others I am testing the genuineness of your love as well.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ: that though he was rich, for your sake he became poor, so that you by his poverty might become rich.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And in this matter I am giving my opinion, for this is to your advantage, you who since last year had already made a beginning not only in doing but also in wanting to.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now complete the doing as well, so that your eagerness in wanting may be matched by your completing it, out of what you have.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For if the eagerness is there, it is acceptable according to what one has, not according to what one does not have.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For this is not so that others may have relief and you affliction, but as a matter of equality:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: at the present time your surplus supplies their lack, so that their surplus may in turn supply your lack, and so there may be equality,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: as it is written:

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “The one who had much did not have too much, and the one who had little did not have too little.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But thanks be to God, who puts the same earnestness for you into the heart of Titus,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for he accepted our urging, and, being more earnest still, he is setting out to you of his own accord.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: With him we are sending the brother whose praise in the good news has spread through all the assemblies—

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and not only that, but he has also been chosen by the assemblies as our traveling companion with this act of grace that is being administered by us, for the glory of the Lord himself and to show our eagerness—

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: we are taking this precaution so that no one may find fault with us over this lavish gift that is being administered by us,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for we give thought to what is honorable not only before the Lord but also before people.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And with them we are sending our brother, whom we have often tested in many matters and found earnest, and who is now much more earnest because of his great confidence in you.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As for Titus, he is my partner and fellow worker for you; as for our brothers, they are envoys of the assemblies, the glory of Christ.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So show them the proof of your love and of our boasting about you, in full view of the assemblies.

notes.note: The Greek word was the ordinary term for a civic gathering and the Septuagint's word for Israel assembled. 'Church' is the near-universal rendering and readers know what it refers to, but it now suggests a building or an institution. 'Assembly' is used throughout this translation so that the one Greek word is visible as one word.

A single Greek word, charis, runs through this chapter and ties it together: God's 'grace' (v. 1), the 'favor' of taking part (v. 4), the collection itself as an 'act of grace' (vv. 6, 7, 19), the 'grace' of Christ (v. 9) and 'thanks' to God (v. 16). English cannot keep one word for all of these, but a Greek reader heard Paul presenting the Corinthians' gift as a response in kind to what God had given.

The Greek plural, used to address a mixed community, was understood to include the women in it. Older translations have 'brethren' or 'brothers'; many recent ones use 'brothers and sisters'. Where the word refers to particular men, as in verses 18, 22 and 23, it is rendered 'brother' or 'brothers'.

The word's basic sense is singleness or sincerity: giving with no ulterior motive and nothing held back. In contexts of giving, most translators and lexicons take it to shade into open-handedness, and that is followed here. Some scholars prefer 'sincerity' or 'single-minded devotion'.

notes.phrase: they gave of their own accord
notes.traditional: they gave of their own accord
notes.note: Paul's sentence in verses 3 to 5 has no main verb until 'they gave themselves' in verse 5; 'they gave' is supplied here, as in most translations, to make the English run. 'Of their own accord' could instead be attached to what follows: 'of their own accord they begged us'.

The word describes all members of the community as people set apart for God, echoing the Septuagint's language for Israel. 'Saints' now suggests canonised individuals or people of exceptional virtue; some translations use 'God's people'. Here it refers to the believers in Jerusalem, for whom the collection was being raised.

notes.phrase: the love from us that is in you
notes.note: The manuscripts are divided between 'the love from us in you' and 'the love from you in us', which would mean 'your love for us'. The text translated here follows the first reading, which is the harder one and is adopted by the main critical editions; many translations follow the second.

notes.phrase: “The one who had much did not have too much, and the one who had little did not have too little.”
notes.note: The quotation is from Exodus 16:18, about the manna in the wilderness: however much or little each person gathered, everyone ended up with enough. Paul uses it as a picture of resources evened out among God's people.

The Greek verbs here and in verses 18 and 22 ('we are sending') are past tenses. Most interpreters take them as the letter-writer's convention of adopting the reader's point of view, since Titus and the brothers probably carried this letter; hence the English present. It is possible, though less likely, that they had already left.

The Greek was an ordinary word for a public announcement of good news. 'Gospel' has become a religious term and a book title, so 'good news' is used throughout this translation; many modern versions alternate between the two.

Paul does not name this brother or the one in verse 22, presumably because the Corinthians would meet them when the letter arrived. Guesses since antiquity have included Luke, Barnabas and others, but his identity is unknown.

The Greek word is the one elsewhere translated 'apostles'. Here it has its ordinary sense of people sent as authorised representatives, in this case by the assemblies, to accompany the collection. Most translations use 'messengers' or 'representatives'; 'envoys' conveys that they carry delegated authority.

candidates.rendering: grace / act of grace / favor / thanks
candidates.reason: One Greek word covers divine grace, a favor, a gift and thanks, and Paul plays on all of them; the register should fix which English is used for each sense so the links stay visible across books.

candidates.rendering: brothers and sisters (plural address); brother (specific men)
candidates.reason: The plural address recurs in every letter and translators split between 'brothers' and 'brothers and sisters'; readers will notice if it varies.
The non-technical sense (here and Philippians 2:25) needs a fixed rendering distinct from 'apostle' with a standard note that the word is the same.
Translators vary between 'ministry', 'service' and 'relief', and 'ministry' now suggests clerical office; a single decision would keep the collection passages and others consistent.
Recurs across the New Testament as 'tribulation', 'affliction', 'trouble', 'distress' or 'hardship', and varying it hides a thematic word.

patch.reason: euangelion promoted to active after full-run drift (good news 37 / gospel 35)
